1.title: Inside Cover - Elijah Muhammad's Signature & Ownership
1.translationMaulana: Dedication and shipment inscription: this Qur'an was sent FROM Mustopa Milham (1559 Central Avenue, Cincinnati, Ohio) TO Elijah Mohammed (6116 South Michigan Avenue, Chicago, Illinois).
1.translationYusuf: The handwritten signature and address of Elijah Muhammad authenticate this as his personal copy of the First Quran given to him by Master Fard Muhammad. This manuscript represents the spiritual foundation upon which the Nation of Islam was built and the guidance the Honorable Elijah Muhammad followed in his ministry to Black America.
1.transliteration: Mustopa Milham / 1559 Central Ave / Cincinnati, Ohio — to — Elijah Mohammed / 6116 S. Michigan Ave. / Chicago, Ill.

مصطفیٰ محمد درہ

Mustopa Milham
1559 Central ave
Cincinnati Ohio

6116 S. Michigan Ave.
Chicago ILL.

2.title: Surah Al-Fatihah (The Opening) - Verse 1 of 7
2.translationMaulana: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.
2.translationYusuf: In the name of Allah, Most Gracious, Most Merciful.
2.annotations: The Basmala opens every action in Islamic practice. Ar-Rahman refers to mercy embracing all creation. Ar-Rahim refers to mercy toward believers. This invocation reconnects the believer to divine guidance and establishes that all derives from Allah's mercy.

3.title: Surah Al-Fatihah (The Opening) - Verse 2 of 7
3.translationMaulana: All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds,
3.translationYusuf: Praise be to Allah, the Cherisher and Sustainer of the worlds;
3.annotations: Al-Hamdu declares that every commendation and gratitude belongs exclusively to Allah. This verse liberates the Black believer from psychological bondage by establishing that true authority flows only from Allah.

4.title: Surah Al-Fatihah (The Opening) - Verse 3 of 7
4.annotations: Ar-Rahman represents universal mercy extended to all creatures. Ar-Rahim represents specific mercy toward believers. This distinction teaches that divine justice operates on two levels: natural law and revealed guidance.

5.title: Surah Al-Fatihah (The Opening) - Verse 4 of 7
5.translationMaulana: Master of the Day of Judgment.
5.translationYusuf: Master of the Day of Judgment.
5.annotations: Malik emphasizes Allah's absolute authority over the Day of Judgment. This verse pivots from mercy to justice, declaring that earthly oppression is temporary while divine justice is eternal.

6.title: Surah Al-Fatihah (The Opening) - Verse 5 of 7
6.translationMaulana: Thee do we serve and Thee do we beseech for help.
6.translationYusuf: Thee do we worship, and Thine aid we seek;
6.annotations: Na'abudu encompasses every act of obedience and submission. The dual repetition creates absolute exclusivity: no other entity deserves worship and no other source provides true assistance.

7.title: Surah Al-Fatihah (The Opening) - Verse 6 of 7
7.translationMaulana: Guide us on the right path,
7.annotations: Ihdina is an urgent request for ongoing divine direction. This verse moves from declaration to supplication, acknowledging that guidance requires constant prayer and seeking from Allah.

8.title: Surah Al-Fatihah (The Opening) - Verse 7 of 7
8.translationMaulana: The path of those upon whom Thou hast bestowed favors. Not (the path) of those upon whom Thy wrath is brought down, nor of those who go astray.
8.translationYusuf: The way of those on whom Thou hast bestowed Thy Grace, those whose (portion) is not wrath, and who go not astray.
8.transliteration: Sirata alladhina an'amta alayhim ghayri al-maghdubi alayhim wa la ad-dallin
8.annotations: Three categories: those upon whom favors are bestowed (the righteous), those upon whom wrath is brought down (arrogant rejectors), and those who go astray (ignorant ones). The believer asks for the righteous path while avoiding arrogance and ignorance.

9.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 1 of 286
9.annotations: Opening with disconnected letters representing coded divine communication. Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest chapter addressing believers, hypocrites, and disbelievers throughout human history.

10.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 2 of 286
10.translationMaulana: This is the Book; there is no doubt in it; it is a guidance to the devout,
10.translationYusuf: This is the Book; in it is guidance sure, without doubt, to those who fear Allah;
10.transliteration: Dhalika al-kitabu la rayba fihi hudan lil-muttaqin
10.annotations: Dhalika al-kitab affirms the Quran as unified and complete. La rayba fih establishes absolute certainty in its divine origin. Guidance is accessed through taqwa—consciousness of Allah and commitment to righteousness.

11.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 3 of 286
11.translationMaulana: Those who believe in the unseen and keep up prayer and spend out of what We have given them,
11.translationYusuf: Who believe in the Unseen, are steadfast in prayer, and spend out of what We have provided for them;
11.transliteration: Al-ladhina yu'minuna bil-ghaybi wa yuqimuna as-salata wa mimma razaqnahum yunfiqun
11.annotations: Three characteristics of believers: belief in the Unseen (accepting divine realities), prayer (disciplined practice five times daily), and spending (charitable giving). These create an integrated believer: spiritually conscious, disciplined, and generous.

12.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 4 of 286
12.translationMaulana: And who believe in that which has been revealed to thee and that which was revealed before thee, and they are sure of the Hereafter.
12.translationYusuf: And who believe in the Revelation sent to thee, and sent before thy time, and (in their hearts) have the assurance of the Hereafter.
12.transliteration: Wa al-ladhina yu'minuna bima unzila ilayka wa ma unzila min qablika wa bil-akhirati hum yaqinun
12.annotations: True faith encompasses all revelation and certainty in the Hereafter. This acknowledges continuity of revelation while accepting the Quran as its culmination and completion.

13.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 5 of 286
13.translationMaulana: These are on a guidance from their Lord, and these are the successful ones.
13.translationYusuf: They are on (true) guidance, from their Lord, and it is these who will prosper.
13.transliteration: Ulaika ala hudan min rabbihim wa ulaika hum al-muflihun
13.annotations: Believers are described as guided and successful through the three characteristics. Success is not merely material but spiritual elevation and eternal reward achieved through alignment with divine order.

14.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 6 of 286
14.translationMaulana: As to those who reject Faith, it is the same to them whether thou warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.
14.translationYusuf: As to those who reject Faith, it is the same to them whether thou warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.
14.transliteration: Inna al-ladhina kafaru sawa alayhi aanzartahum am lam tanzarhum la yu'minun
14.annotations: Those who reject faith are closed-minded because they willfully reject and suppress truth. The believer's responsibility is to convey the message, not force acceptance of those determined to disbelieve.

15.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 7 of 286
15.translationMaulana: Allah hath set a seal on their hearts and on their hearing, and on their eyes is a veil; and for them is a great chastisement.
15.translationYusuf: Allah hath set a seal on their hearts and on their hearing, and on their eyes is a veil; and for them is a great chastisement.
15.transliteration: Khatama Allahu ala qulubihim wa ala sam'ihim wa ala absar ihim ghishawatun wa lahum azabun azim
15.annotations: Spiritual sealing results from persistent rejection. The person's choice eventually closes their capacity to receive it. This sealing follows rejection; the message remains available to those not yet sealed.

16.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 8 of 286
16.translationMaulana: And there are some people who say: We believe in Allah and the last day; and they are not believers.
16.translationYusuf: And there are some people who say: "We believe in Allah and the Last Day;" but they do not (really) believe.
16.transliteration: Wa min al-nasi man yaqulu amanna billahi wa bil-yawmi al-akhiri wa ma hum bimu'minin
16.annotations: Hypocrites claim faith while harboring disbelief, occupying a middle ground for personal advantage. They are more dangerous than open disbelievers because deception destabilizes community and obscures truth.

17.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 9 of 286
17.translationMaulana: They try to deceive Allah and those who believe, and they deceive only themselves and they do not perceive.
17.translationYusuf: Fain would they deceive Allah and those who believe, but they only deceive themselves, and realise (it) not.
17.transliteration: Yukhadi'una Allaha wa al-ladhina amanu wa ma yakhda'una illa anfusahum wa ma yash'urun
17.annotations: Self-deception is inherent in hypocrisy. One cannot deceive Allah or the faithful—only oneself. The consequences of deception fall primarily on the deceiver who damages their own soul.

18.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 10 of 286
18.translationMaulana: In their hearts is a disease, so Allah hath increased their disease; and for them is a painful chastisement because they lie.
18.translationYusuf: In their hearts is a disease; and Allah has increased their disease: And grievous is the chastisement they (incur), because they are false (to themselves).
18.transliteration: Fi qulubihim maradun fa-zadahumu Allahu marada wa lahum azabun alimun bima kanu yakdhiun
18.annotations: Spiritual disease characterizes the hypocrite through doubt, corruption, and moral weakness. Continued hypocrisy compounds spiritual sickness—each deceptive act further corrupts the soul.

19.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 11 of 286
19.translationMaulana: [Verse 2:11 - Maulana Muhammad Ali (1934 Public Domain Translation)]
19.annotations: Hypocrite's justification of destructive behavior through false claims of reform. The tactic is claiming noble intentions while pursuing selfish or divisive ends that actually weaken collective power.

20.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 12 of 286
20.translationMaulana: [Verse 2:12 - Maulana Muhammad Ali (1934 Public Domain Translation)]
20.annotations: Revelation of hypocrite's true nature: corruption flows from their own actions, yet they remain trapped in delusion. Reality is objective: actions produce effects regardless of profession or claimed intent.

21.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 13 of 286
21.translationMaulana: [Verse 2:13 - Maulana Muhammad Ali (1934 Public Domain Translation)]
21.annotations: Arrogance of hypocrite who rejects faith by scorning the faithful as foolish. The one calling believers foolish is actually foolish and cannot see their own spiritual blindness.

22.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 14 of 286
22.translationMaulana: [Verse 2:14 - Maulana Muhammad Ali (1934 Public Domain Translation)]
22.annotations: Hypocrite's dual behavior: professing faith to believers while mocking faith to the wicked. Complete compartmentalization reveals true loyalty is to exploiters and oppressive forces.

23.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 15 of 286
23.translationMaulana: [Verse 2:15 - Maulana Muhammad Ali (1934 Public Domain Translation)]
23.annotations: Divine justice mirrors the hypocrite's mocking through exposure of their deception. Allah gives rope to the wicked to hang themselves, allowing destructive course until consequences become undeniable.

24.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 16 of 286
24.translationMaulana: [Verse 2:16 - Maulana Muhammad Ali (1934 Public Domain Translation)]
24.annotations: Economic language reveals spiritual exchange—hypocrite trades away guidance for error at great loss. This exchange yields no benefit; the hypocrite remains lost despite attempts to navigate.

25.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 17 of 286
25.translationMaulana: [Verse 2:17 - Maulana Muhammad Ali (1934 Public Domain Translation)]
25.annotations: Parable describing trajectory: initial apparent advantage followed by complete loss. The fire kindles brightly then is extinguished, leaving the hypocrite in total darkness without direction.

26.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 18 of 286
26.translationMaulana: [Verse 2:18 - Maulana Muhammad Ali (1934 Public Domain Translation)]
26.annotations: Complete spiritual incapacity of those rejecting guidance repeatedly. The three disabilities (deaf, dumb, blind) describe total spiritual death—faculties atrophy through disuse and willful rejection.

27.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 19 of 286
27.translationMaulana: [Verse 2:19 - Maulana Muhammad Ali (1934 Public Domain Translation)]
27.annotations: Second parable: those encountering truth but rejecting it from fear. They fear accepting truth requires surrender of ego and fundamental change—a death to the old self.

28.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 20 of 286
28.translationMaulana: [Verse 2:20 - Maulana Muhammad Ali (1934 Public Domain Translation)]
28.annotations: Unstable, reactive condition of those encountering truth without commitment. They move forward when evidence is undeniable, then retreat when truth becomes challenging or socially costly.

29.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 21 of 286
29.translationMaulana: [Verse 2:21 - Maulana Muhammad Ali (1934 Public Domain Translation)]
29.annotations: Direct call to worship addressed to all humanity, not limited to one nation. Worship develops taqwa—consciousness of Allah restraining from transgression and liberating the enslaved mind.

30.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 22 of 286
30.translationMaulana: [Verse 2:22 - Maulana Muhammad Ali (1934 Public Domain Translation)]
30.annotations: Evidence of divine providence: earth's habitability, sky's protection, water cycle, earth's productivity. This perfect provision evidences that nothing rivals Allah in power or care.

31.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 23 of 286
31.translationMaulana: [Verse 2:23 - Maulana Muhammad Ali (1934 Public Domain Translation)]
31.annotations: Verse 2:23 - Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow). Juz 1 spans from Surah Al-Fatihah through Surah Al-Baqarah verse 141. Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest chapter of the Quran (286 verses total) and was revealed in Medina. It addresses believers (Al-Muttaqin), hypocrites (Al-Munafiqun), and disbelievers (Al-Kafirun). The Honorable Elijah Muhammad drew extensively from this Surah in teaching the Nation of Islam about divine guidance, community law, spiritual discipline, and the path to salvation for Black people in America.

118.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 110 of 286
118.translationMaulana: Those to whom We gave the Scripture rejoice at what has been revealed to you, but among the factions are those who reject part of it. Say, "I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not associate partners with Him." To Him is my invitation, and to Him will be my return. Say, "Indeed, my Lord throws the truth, and He is the Knower of the unseen."
118.transliteration: Ulá'ik alládhín átaynáhum al-kitáb yafrḥún bi-má unzila ilayka wa-min al-ahzáb man yunkar ba'dah qul innamá umirt an a'bud Alláha wa-lá ushrik bih • Ilayh tadúun wa-huwa al-haqq ta'alá 'ammá yushrikun • Qul inna rabbee yaqdhif bi-al-haqq 'allám al-ghuyúb
118.annotations:
Arabic text on this page:

Verse 53: أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِمَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمِنَ الْأَحْزَابِ مَن يُنكِرُ بَعْضَهُ ۚ قُلْ إِنَّمَا أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ وَلَا أُشْرِكَ بِهِ

Verse 54: إِلَيْهِ تَدْعُونَ وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ تَعَالَىٰ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ

Verse 55: قُلْ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَقْذِفُ بِالْحَقِّ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ

Urdu/Persian tafsir on this page:

جن لوگوں کو ہم نے کتاب دی ہے وہ خوش ہیں اس سے جو تم پر نازل ہوا
— "Those to whom We gave Scripture rejoice at what was revealed to you"

اور فریقوں میں سے کوئی اس کے کچھ حصے کا انکار کرتے ہیں
— "But some factions reject part of it"

کہو میں صرف اللہ کی عبادت کرنے کا حکم دیا گیا ہوں اور اسے شریک نہ کروں
— "Say I am commanded to worship Allah alone and not associate partners"

119.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 111 of 286
119.translationMaulana: Say, "Indeed, Allah does not wrong by even an atom's weight. And if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward." So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you against these people as a witness?
119.transliteration: Qul inna Alláha lá yazlim mithqal dharrah wa-in taku hasanah yudá'ifhá wa-yu'ti min ladunhu ajran 'azímaan • Fa-kayf idha ji'ná min kulli ummah bi-shahíd wa-ji'ná bik 'alá há'ulá'i shahíd
119.annotations:
Arabic text on this page:

Verse 56: قُل إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَظْلِمُ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ ۖ وَإِن تَكُ حَسَنَةً يُضَاعِفْهَا وَيُؤْتِ مِن لَّدُنْهُ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا

Verse 57: فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جِئْنَا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ وَجِئْنَا بِكَ عَلَىٰ هَٰؤُلَاءِ شَهِيدًا

Urdu/Persian tafsir on this page:

کہو اللہ ذرے برابر بھی ظلم نہیں کرتا
— "Say Allah does not wrong even an atom's weight"

اور اگر کوئی نیک کام ہے تو اسے دگنا کرتا ہے اور اپنی طرف سے بڑا اجر دیتا ہے
— "If there is good deed He doubles it and gives great reward from Himself"

تو کیسے ہوگا جب ہم ہر امت سے ایک گواہ لائیں اور تمہیں ان پر گواہ بنائیں
— "How then when We bring a witness from every nation and make you witness against them"

120.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 112 of 286
120.translationMaulana: Those who disbelieve wish that you would disbelieve as they disbelieved so you would be alike. So do not take allies from among them until they emigrate for the cause of Allah — except those who take refuge with a people between you and whom there is a treaty, or those who come to you with hearts disinclined to fight you or to fight their own people.
120.transliteration: Yawud alládhín kafarú law lam takúnu mu'minín wa-ta'khudhun 'alá ayámánih kulla widd qul hal tarabbastun bina illá iḥdá al-ḥusnayin • Illá alládhín yasilun ilá qawm baynakum wa-baynahum míthaq aw já'úkum qásírah sudúruhum an yuqátilukum aw yuqátilú qawmahum
120.annotations:
Arabic text on this page:

Verse 58: يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْ لَمْ تَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ وَتَأْخُذُونَ عَلَىٰ أَيْمَانِهِمْ كُلَّ وِدٍّ ۚ قُلْ هَلْ تَرَبَّصُونَ بِنَا إِلَّا إِحْدَى الْحُسْنَيَيْنِ

Verse 59: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُم مِّيثَاقٌ أَوْ جَاءُوكُم قَاسِرَةً صُدُورُهُمْ أَن يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ أَوْ يُقَاتِلُوا قَوْمَهُمْ

Urdu/Persian tafsir on this page:

کافر چاہتے ہیں کہ کاش تم بھی کافر ہوتے تاکہ برابر ہوتے
— "Those who disbelieve wish you were disbelievers so you'd be equal"

تو ان میں سے اپنے حلیف نہ بناؤ جب تک وہ اللہ کے راستے میں ہجرت نہ کریں
— "So do not take allies from them until they emigrate for Allah's sake"

سوائے ان لوگوں کے جو ایسی قوم سے ملے ہوں جن سے تمہارا معاہدہ ہے
— "Except those joined to a people with whom you have a treaty"

121.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 113 of 286
121.translationMaulana: And when We intend to destroy a city, We command its affluent people, and they commit defilement in it; so the word comes into effect upon it, and We destroy it with complete destruction. And how many prophets We sent among the former peoples.
121.transliteration: Wa-idha aradná an nuhlík qaryah amrná mutrafíhá fa-fasaqu fíhá fa-ḥaqqa 'alayha al-qawl fa-dammarná ha tadmíran • Wa-kam arsalná min nabíy fi-al-awwalín

126.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 118 of 286
126.translationMaulana: And when a faction of them said, "Why do you advise a people whom Allah is about to destroy or to punish with a severe punishment?" 141.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 133 of 286
141.translationMaulana: And hold firmly to the rope of Allah, all together, and do not become divided. And remember the favor of Allah upon you — when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together, so you became, by His favor, brothers. And you were on the edge of a pit of the Fire, and He saved you from it. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses that you may be guided.
141.transliteration: Wa-i'tasmu bi-ḥabl Alláhi jamí'an wa-lá tafarraqu wa-idhkuru ni'mat Alláhi 'alaykum idh kuntum a'dá' fa-allaif bayn qulúbikum fa-asbḥtum bi-ni'matih ikhwánan • Wa-kuntum 'alá shafá ḥufrah min an-nár fa-anqadhákum minhá kadhálika yubayyín Alláhu lakum ayátih la'allakum tahtadun

— "And you were on the edge of a pit of Fire and He saved you from it"

142.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 134 of 286
142.translationMaulana: You are the best nation produced as an example for mankind. You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in Allah. If only the People of the Scripture had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient. They will not harm you except for some annoyance. And if they fight you, they will turn their backs to you; then they will not be aided.
142.transliteration: Kuntum khayra ummah ukhríjat li-an-nás ta'murun bi-al-ma'ruf wa-tahawn 'an al-munkar wa-tu'minun bi-Alláhi wa-law ámana ahl al-kitáb la-kán khayran lahum minhum al-mu'minun wa-aktharu hum al-fásiqun • Lan yadukkum illá adhan wa-in yuqátilukum yuwallúkum al-adbár thumma lá yunsarun

143.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 135 of 286
143.translationMaulana: Neither those who disbelieved from the People of the Scripture nor the polytheists wish that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord. But Allah selects for His mercy whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty. Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees. And Allah is Aware of what you do.
143.transliteration: Má yawud alládhín kafarú min ahl al-kitáb wa-lá al-mushrikín an yunazal 'alaykum min khayrin min rabbkum wa-Alláhu yakhtas bi-raḥmatih man yasháa wa-Alláhu dhú al-fadl al-'azím • Rafa' Alláhu alládhín ámanú minkum wa-alládhín útú al-'ilm darajat wa-Alláhu bi-má ta'malun khabír

— "Allah chooses His mercy for whom He wills and Allah has immense bounty"

144.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - Verse 136 of 286
144.translationMaulana: We do not abrogate any verse or cause it to be forgotten except that We bring forth one better than it or similar to it. Do you not know that Allah is over all things competent? Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that you have not besides Allah any patron or any helper? Or do you intend to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before? And whoever exchanges faith for disbelief has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way.
144.transliteration: Má nansakh min áyah aw nunisihá na'ti bi-khayrin minhá aw mithlihá alam ta'lam anna Alláha 'alá kulli shay' qadír • Alam ta'lam anna Alláha lahu mulk as-samawat wa-al-ard wa-má lakum min dun Alláhi min walíy wa-lá nasír • Am turídun an tas'alú rasúlakum kamá su'ila músá min qabl wa-man yatabaddal al-kufr bi-al-íman fa-qad dálla sawá' as-sabíl
